html:
Sanjaasürengiin Zorig (1962 to 1998) was a leader of Mongolia's peaceful democratic revolution of 1990, remembered as the Golden Swallow of Democracy. A young lecturer at the national university in Ulaanbaatar, he helped found the Mongolian Democratic Union in December 1989.

Through the winter of 1989 to 1990 he led rallies and hunger strikes in the central square of the capital, and he is remembered for keeping the protests peaceful. In March 1990 the communist leadership resigned, and that summer Mongolia held its first free elections. Zorig was elected to parliament and took part in shaping the constitution of 1992.

In 1998 he was minister of infrastructure and was expected to become prime minister. On 2 October that year he was stabbed to death in his home in Ulaanbaatar. The murder went unsolved for years; men were convicted only in 2016, in a closed trial, and many questions remain. His statue stands in the centre of the capital.
